To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The world copper industry between 1870 and 1930 was characterized by the rise of large corporations, and (ii) this rise was due to technological imperatives rather than to transactional considerations.

the large firm in the mining and refining sectors of the copper business is a response to technology and the need for large scale operations, and the large firm in copper fabricating is a response to the market and the need for vertical integration.

the growth of big copper firms resulted in a significant increase in the efficiency of the industry, and that the growth of these companies was driven largely by the need for large-scale capital investment, and not by the desire to exploit monopoly power.
